[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intros?
[00:08] Dana: Dana Brooks, head of ML at Cynosure. We run a search+recommendation product and want to evaluate Redwood for low-latency generation and reranking.
[00:15] Amit: Amit here, platform eng, I'll be the primary infra contact.
[00:19] Kelsey: Kelsey, PM owning the use-case and success criteria.
[00:24] Lina: Lina, solutions engineer at Redwood, I'll lead benchmarks and integration guidance. Marco: Marco here for performance questions.

[00:40] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to agree on success criteria, understand workload shape, and pick a bench plan and timeline plus integration questions around SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

[00:52] Dana: From our side, top things are latency: 99th percentile under 250ms for short prompts if possible, cost per inference, and no regressions in quality compared to our current actor. We also need to know deployment options, e.g., hosted vs VPC for prod.
[01:12] Kelsey: And timeline: we'd like a working POC in ~2 weeks, with benchmarks in week 2, and a decision by mid-June.

[01:28] Lina: Cool. Can you walk us through your current traffic and model use? Typical sequence lengths, tokens per request, and concurrency?
[01:36] Amit: Sure. Our current inference mix: about 3k QPS at peak across global regions, but the pilot will be much smaller targeting 100-200 QPS per region. Average prompt length is ~60 tokens, responses around 120 tokens. Long tail up to 800 tokens for some analytical flows.

[02:02] Marco: When you say 100-200 QPS for pilot, is that steady or spiky?
[02:06] Amit: Expect spiky bursts to 400 for a minute or two.

[02:12] Lina: That helps. For the POC we'll suggest running a representative 5k-10k query workload with both steady and burst traffic in the benchmark. We'll instrument latency p50/p95/p99 and token cost.

[02:30] Dana: On quality, we have a set of 200 prompts we use for regression tests. We'd want Redwood to run those and match baseline metrics: top-1 accuracy for reranking and a manual review tolerance for generation.

[02:48] Jordan: Good, so success criteria: latency p99 < 250ms (short prompts), cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll propose), and no >5% regressions on your 200-prompt eval set.

[03:05] Kelsey: That sounds right. Also we need structured output for a subset of prompts — JSON schema enforcement is important. We saw Redwood mentions structured output support; how would that work?

[03:20] Lina: Redwood supports structured output in two ways: model-side deterministic parsing with schema hints and a post-processing validator in the SDK that can enforce and reject invalid responses. For the POC we'll show an example with the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and SDK that returns a JSON blob and an explicit confidence flag.

[03:40] Amit: SDK—do you have official SDKs? We currently use an OpenAI-compatible client library so compatibility is important.

[03:47] Jordan: Yes, official SDKs in Python, Node, and Java, plus an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint that maps standard params. For function/tool calling we support the same style: you can register a function schema, call the model and get back structured arguments.

[04:05] Marco: Quick note: our OpenAI-compatible endpoint has a couple idiosyncrasies: some of the param names differ, and streaming semantics can slightly vary. We'll share docs.

[04:16] Kelsey: On tool calling: we want to chain the LLM with our internal tools for retrieval and enrichment. Any special integration pieces?

[04:24] Lina: For tool/function calling, we support the function-calling spec. You can declare functions in the SDK; during the POC we can demo a retrieval-augmented flow where the model returns a function call to your retrieval service. It works with both hosted and private deployments.

[04:42] Dana: Security: we require SOC2-like assurances and SSO. If the POC is hosted, we need to ensure logs can be limited. For production, we'd likely want VPC or private deployment.

[04:55] Jordan: We can provide SOC 2 reports and SSO/SAML support. Hosted POC will have audit logs; for production VPC/private options are supported but will have a longer lead time. We'll put that in the SOW.

[05:10] Amit: For benchmarks, what's the plan? Are you willing to run in our dev env or run Redwood-hosted benchmarks against a sample dataset?

[05:18] Lina: Both are options. Preferred is: you provide a dev endpoint or sample dataset and we run the benchmarks in Redwood's environment to measure our stack end-to-end; alternatively we can supply a benchmark harness you run against your infra. For the POC we recommend Redwood-run to control variables.

[05:36] Kelsey: How about measuring cost—do you show raw token counts and cost by model variant?

[05:42] Marco: Yes, Console reports token breakdown, cost per route/model, and trace-level latency. For the benchmark we'll export a CSV and a short dashboard.

[05:53] Dana: We want to test quantized variants too, like 4-bit models, to see cost tradeoffs. Does Redwood support quantized model variants and automatic fallback?

[06:02] Lina: We support quantized models and can route to cheaper variants with comparable quality. For the POC we can include one quantized run and one full-precision run. There is a small chance of quality delta; we'll track regression.

[06:17] Jordan: Ok, so concretely for the benchmark we'll run: baseline run (your 200 eval prompts), steady 100 QPS run, burst test up to 400 QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and structured-output schema validation pass rate.

[06:35] Amit: Sounds good. How long will the benchmark run take?

[06:38] Lina: The harness itself is 2 hours for a full run but we'll need prep time to load keys and datasets — expect 3-4 hours total including setup and analysis.

[06:48] Kelsey: For the POC success criteria, we should list thresholds. I'll propose: p99 < 350ms for mixed prompts but p99 < 250ms for short prompts <100 tokens; quality regression <=5% on our eval; structured-output parse >95%; cost savings target 20% vs current infra. Does that sound feasible?

[07:14] Marco: Reasonable targets for a pilot. We'll try to hit 250ms p99 but some tail at 350ms during bursts is possible depending on batch windows. We can tune batch/latency trade-offs.

[07:28] Dana: On integration — how intrusive is switching to Redwood SDKs? We prefer minimal code changes.

[07:33] Jordan: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint means you can often swap URLs and keys with minimal code changes. Our SDKs have helpers for structured output and function calling that mirror OpenAI-style calls. We'll share sample diffs in the repo link.

[07:48] Amit: CI/CD—do you offer a canary rollout with fallback? We need graceful degradation so our product doesn't go down if the model has issues.

[07:56] Lina: Yes, our routing supports canary and automatic fallback to a cheaper model or a static response. We can configure per-route policies in the console.

[08:06] Kelsey: For data residency and key management—do you integrate with customer KMS or HSM in private deploy?

[08:12] Lina: For Private deployments we integrate with KMS/HSM and you manage keys. For Hosted we offer integration with major KMS providers for key wrapping and customer-managed keys for an extra tier.

[08:25] Jordan: Quick pragmatic questions — what's your internal approval path? Who signs the SOW?

[08:30] Kelsey: I'll own the internal decision; procurement will sign. Expect formal review by our infra/security folks after the POC.

[08:38] Dana: One more: we need a sample structured output schema example during the POC. Can you provide a template?

[08:44] Lina: Yes, we'll include a JSON schema example and an SDK snippet showing function spec -> model -> structured JSON result. We'll also include a validation hook you can run in CI.

[08:58] Jordan: Ok let's put timeline on the table: Jordan to send SOW by Monday (2026-05-24). Customer to share sample dataset and dev access by Friday (2026-05-28). Benchmark run week of 2026-05-26, follow-up 2026-06-02. Decision mid-June.

[09:16] Amit: For the dev access, we'll provide a simple API key and a small sandbox cluster; do you need VPC peering for POC?

[09:22] Lina: Not for the hosted POC. If you want Redwood to run tests inside your VPC we can set up Private POC but that adds setup time — estimated 2-3 weeks. For initial evaluation hosted is faster.

[09:36] Kelsey: Ok we'll do hosted POC first. If successful we'll scope VPC for prod.

[09:42] Jordan: Perfect. Any blockers today?

[09:45] Dana: No blockers. Will need to confirm the eval prompts and stakeholders.

[09:50] Kelsey: I'll circulate success criteria doc after this call and confirm stakeholders by 2026-05-25.

[09:58] Jordan: Great. Lina, Marco — you two will own the bench plan and run?

[10:02] Lina: Yep, we'll own it. We'll draft a benchmark harness and test scripts and share in the repo.

[10:09] Marco: I'll focus on performance tuning, batching and quantization knobs.

[10:14] Dana: One last logistical question — are there rate limit considerations or quotas for the POC?

[10:19] Jordan: We'll provision a POC tier to support the bursts — no enforced throttling at those volumes for the short duration of the benchmark. We'll define quotas in the SOW.

[10:28] Kelsey: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

Jordan to send SOW/pricing; Lina to prepare benchmark plan and SDK samples; Amit to share dataset and dev access; Kelsey to confirm success criteria and stakeholders. We'll reconvene 2026-06-02 to review benchmark outputs. Links: SOW draft (link to shared doc), benchmark spreadsheet (link), SDK repo snippet (link).
